sections.content: You know the *pluscuamperfecto* from B1 Unit 1: *había* + past participle says that something had already happened before another moment in the past. In the story of the revolution it shows what the rebels had already done when something else happened: *cuando Batista huyó, los rebeldes ya habían ganado importantes batallas*.

items.spanish: Cuando Batista huyó, los rebeldes ya habían ganado importantes batallas.
items.english: When Batista fled, the rebels had already won important battles.

items.spanish: Los rebeldes que habían sobrevivido se refugiaron en la Sierra Maestra.
items.english: The rebels who had survived took refuge in the Sierra Maestra.

items.spanish: Che Guevara era un médico argentino que había llegado a Cuba en el Granma.
items.english: Che Guevara was an Argentine doctor who had come to Cuba on the Granma.

items.spanish: Castro había salido de la cárcel en 1955 y vivía en México.
items.english: Castro had left prison in 1955 and was living in Mexico.

sections.content: Use the pluperfect for the earlier action and the preterite for the later one: *cuando huyó Batista* (later), *ya habían ganado* (earlier). Nothing goes between *había* and the participle: *ya habían ganado*, not *habían ya ganado*.
